verdict.rationale: Docusign's official eSignature REST API and Node client support signing via API ('Send, sign, and approve documents using this client'). Hands-on community reports confirm developers build embedded signing by generating embedded envelope signing URLs, one calling it 'fairly seamless'. One older report describes users breaking out of the embedded signing page, with the fix requiring a legacy API version; another developer reports the opposite experience. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of embedded signing (iframe/recipient-view flow, branding of the embedded session) in the pack, and current evidence that the embedded session-isolation issue is resolved.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed the signing experience inside my own app or website

citations.quote: The Official Docusign Node.js Client Library used to interact with the eSign REST API. Send, sign, and approve documents using this client.
We use the v2 REST API creating embedded envelope signing URLs without issues.
We did exactly this embedded signing integration and it was fairly seamless
